newsitem.title: PERU: Peru government will not give in to rebels-report.
newsitem.headline: Peru government will not give in to rebels-report.

text.p: The Peruvian government refused on Friday to give in to demands made by leftist rebels holding nearly 400 men hostage in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, according to a local television report.
"The aggrement is to approve the president's proposal to not accept the demand to release terrorists held in Peru's jails," the Panamericana television station said.
The report could not immediately be confirmed.

About 20 guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have threatened to kill the hostages, including high-ranking diplomats, foreign businessmen and top government officials, if Peru does not release up to 500 of their imprisoned comrades.
Tentative negotations with the rebels have produced no apparent progress although about 100 women and elderly were released by the rebels at the start of the crisis.

Peru's President Alberto Fujimori promised in a letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton that the safety of the hostages would be his first priority in resolving the siege. Fujimori met with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda late Thursday to discuss options for ending the 3-day-old standoff.
